_comment: Single source of truth for workflow SHAPE (the third axis). The task-type registry says what each node SAYS (routing + workflow prose); the verify-mode registry says what each phase gate MEANS; THIS registry says the node SEQUENCE — which agents a workflow runs, in what order, its verify policy, and its stop condition. The fixed state machine's topology (planner -> executor -> checker) becomes DECLARED here, so a project ships a custom shape (e.g. research-first) with zero plugin edits. dispatch.py reads this via track_state.workflow_shapes — an action outside the resolved shape's `nodes` is refused (the lightest touch that makes the shape load-bearing without rewriting the action-driven spine). Adding a shape = one row here, zero Python edits. A project may overlay conductor/workflow/workflow-shapes.json (opt-in by file presence) to add or override shapes with zero plugin edits.

_fields.nodes: the ordered list of dispatch agents this shape runs (the topology). Action tokens: spec-planner | explorer | task-executor | phase-checker | test-runner | ac-tracer. dispatch.py refuses an action whose agent is not in this list when the shape is resolved.
_fields.requires: optional prerequisites the shape demands of track-state before it can run (advisory; future hook). Absent => no prerequisites.
_fields.verify_policy: how this shape gates progress: checkpoint (the default — phase-checker stamps a checkpoint gate) | none (no checkpoint gate — research/exploration shapes that produce no committable artifact).
_fields.stop_condition: what makes the shape DONE: all_nodes_done (every node in `nodes` has run) | a structured pass_condition. The fixed spine's default is all_nodes_done.
_fields.instruction: optional prompt-shaping prose for the orchestrator when this shape is active (mirrors the task-type `workflow` + verify-mode `protocol` fields). Absent => the orchestrator follows the default §3.0 dispatch loop.

default.instruction: The standard implement loop: spec-planner decomposes the brief into a plan, task-executor implements each task under the TDD/coverage gates, phase-checker verifies each phase and stamps the checkpoint. This is the shape the conductor has always run — declared here so it is data-driven, not hardcoded.

research-first.when_to_use: A track whose first need is understanding — map the codebase / survey a dependency / spike an approach BEFORE planning. Runs explorer first, feeds its findings into spec-planner, then implements. No checkpoint gate (exploration produces no committable artifact to verify).
research-first.instruction: Research-first shape: dispatch explorer FIRST to map the relevant subsystem and record findings to the handoff. spec-planner then decomposes the brief WITH the exploration findings in hand (richer plan). task-executor implements. No phase-checker checkpoint — exploration is not a committable artifact, so verify_policy is none.
